column1: # signatures.tsv — the fetch/transport signature table FR-005 owns.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   kind      retry | noretry | nomatch
#   pattern   ERE matched against the attempt's whole log
#   sample    a concrete log line the pattern must match — the selftest's
#             printer prints this; the row IS its own case by construction.
#             A `nomatch` row inverts the contract: the selftest asserts the
#             pattern does NOT match the sample and the run classifies
#             `unclassified` at 1 attempt — the gate ignores the kind, so the
#             row exists purely as a pinned negative.
# The harness feeds one sample per run, so rows prove per-row behavior only —
# cross-signature interaction (a log matching a retry row AND a noretry row,
# where exclusion must win) is covered solely by the two hand-authored
# precedence rows near the bottom, not by construction.
#   retry   — a match is a network flake: wipe cleanup-dirs, retry.
#   noretry — auth-shaped output: fails fast EVEN when a retry pattern also
#             matches; exclusion is checked before inclusion (a dead
#             credential must never burn three attempts).
# `RPC failed` is never a bare signature: unqualified it also matches auth
# rejections — the failures meant to fail fast — so it is always written
# transport-scoped (a curl code or an HTTP 5xx).
# `Could not resolve host` retries a mistyped manifest host twice more
# before failing with the real code — the accepted cost of matching DNS
# failures at all.
retry

column1: # `Couldn’t fetch updates…` is SwiftPM's wrapper for its internal
# cache-update git fetch — emitted with U+2019, so the pattern matches
# `Could.*` rather than the apostrophe byte. It must also anchor at line
# start: the same words arrive non-fatally inside
# `warning: skipping cache due to an error: …`, where resolution falls
# back and continues — matching that form would retry any permanent
# failure that merely carried the warning. The fatal second-stage-resolve
# surface this row exists for prints the summary on its own line —
# observed verbatim in run 41185222185's `KernelApp (ios)` job log, which
# is the sample below (2-space indent, real U+2019 byte). Residual: if a
# formatter ever WRAPS the warning so the summary lands on its own
# indented line, it is indistinguishable from the fatal surface and will
# retry — a line-wise anchor cannot close that; the nomatch row pins the
# single-line form observed today. The permanent companions the fatal
# surface can travel with are excluded below, not retried.
retry

column1: # The permanent deaths the fetch summary can carry — git's non-interactive
# auth failure, a dead package URL (the `#fragment` shape pins this one
# down: bare `info/refs not valid` can also mean a transient proxy/CDN
# error page), and a missing repo — excluded before inclusion by kind
# (the header's precedence rule), not by position. Each pattern is
# anchored on its observed `fatal:`/`remote:` transport marker rather
# than line-start: `matches_any` greps the whole log and exclusion wins
# first, so a bare phrase could match non-fatal wrapper text elsewhere
# and suppress a genuine transport flake; the marker requirement keeps
# the kill precise while staying constructable inside a precedence row.
noretry
